messages.content:
Follow these writing rules. They matter as much as the content:

- Bold used as body emphasis throughout -- reserve bold for a rare callout
- A short rhetorical question with a canned answer -- collapse into one direct statement
- Short buildup, then a reveal: "The best part: it learns." -- state it as a plain sentence
- Emoji or decorative checkmarks in body text -- cut them
- An em dash, section sign or middle dot written as an HTML entity -- write the plain character
- Throat-clearing openers: "needless to say", "at the end of the day" -- state the point directly from the first sentence
- Fake ID tags opening list items: "R-1.", "US-01" -- number the list plainly
- Marketing adjectives: seamless, robust, cutting-edge -- say what is actually true
- The "not just X but Y" construction -- make the point once
- Body paragraphs nearly identical in length -- vary them with what each paragraph has to do
- A significance clause bolted to a sentence: ", underscoring the..." -- delete it, or make it a claim with something behind it
- Three parallel -ing items in a series -- keep the one that carries information
- Fake-humility feedback requests: "would love your feedback on this" -- cut them
- Horizontal rules dropped between sections -- headings already separate sections
- Headings Capitalised Like This -- sentence case
- Vague intensifiers with no number behind them: very, really, quite, significantly -- say how much, or cut the word
- Unnamed authority: "studies show", "experts agree" -- name the actual source, or cut the claim

Now write the following. Return only the requested text.
Write the copy for the pricing page of a code review tool, covering three tiers. Around 250 words.

output:
# Pricing

Three tiers. Every one of them runs the same review engine — the difference is how many repos it watches and who it answers to.

## Solo — $0

For one person and up to three private repos. You get pull request comments on every diff, the full rule set, and the CLI so you can run the same checks locally before you push. No credit card, no trial clock. If you never outgrow it, stay here.

## Team — $18 per developer per month

Unlimited private repos, plus the parts that only matter once more than one person is reading the output. Shared rule configuration lives in a file in your repo, so a rule change goes through review like any other change. Reviews block merges when you tell them to and stay advisory when you don't. You also get the history view: which rules fire most, which ones people dismiss, and which files keep coming back.

Teams above 40 developers get volume pricing; write to sales@example.com with your headcount.

## Enterprise — talk to us

Self-hosted or in your own cloud account, SAML and SCIM, audit logs that export to your SIEM, and a written data processing agreement. You can write custom rules in Python against our AST API and ship them to every repo in the org from one place. Support is a shared Slack channel with a four-hour response target during your business hours.

Annual billing on Team and Enterprise saves two months. Switching down a tier takes effect at the end of the billing period, and your data comes with you either way.
